# Cadet AI

> Cadet AI is an independent study-aid app for UK Army Cadet Force (ACF) and Combined Cadet Force (CCF) cadets aged 13 and over. Its built-in AI assistant, TANGO, answers training questions grounded in the cadet syllabus and is designed not to make things up (it says when it is unsure). The app adds quizzes across 13 subjects from Basic to 4-Star, XP, military ranks, 229 badges, 35 awards, opt-in leaderboards, and read-aloud / matched character voices. It is not an official MOD, ACF, CCF or Cadet Forces product and is not endorsed by them. Available on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/id6802644162 and on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cadetai.app

## Key facts
- Platform: iOS (iPhone and iPad) and Android. Available on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/id6802644162 and on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cadetai.app
- Audience: cadets aged 13+; under-13s cannot create an account. Also useful to parents/guardians and unit staff.
- Pricing: Free "Cadet" plan with 5 TANGO messages and 3 quizzes a day; Plus (£4.99/month or £44.99/year); Pro (£9.99/month or £89.99/year). Monthly Plus and Pro each include a 7-day free trial. No ads, no third-party analytics trackers, data never sold.
- Subjects covered: Drill & Turnout, Fieldcraft & Tactics, First Aid, Navigation, Shooting, Skill at Arms, Military Knowledge, Communications & IT, Expedition & Adventurous Training, Keeping Active, Community Engagement, JCIC / CFIT.
- TANGO: a grounded AI study assistant that sticks to cadet training and won't make things up; 20 characters (the Free plan includes 5, Plus unlocks 15, Pro unlocks all 20); on Plus and Pro each character speaks with its own matched premium voice.
- Privacy: national and unit leaderboards are opt-in and off by default, show a self-chosen nickname only, and are separated so adult volunteers and under-18 cadets never appear on the same board. There is no messaging, following, commenting or photo sharing anywhere in the app.
- Affiliation: NOT affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to the Ministry of Defence, the British Army, the ACF, the CCF or any official cadet organisation. It is an independent study aid built by MonkeyZoo Ltd, a UK company.
- Safety stance: for anything safety-critical or weapons-related, TANGO tells cadets to confirm with a qualified instructor rather than answering definitively.
- Account deletion: users can delete their account and all associated data at any time from Settings in the app.
- Support: support@cadetai.co.uk

## Guides
- [Cadet terms & acronyms explained](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/cadet-terms-and-acronyms.html): glossary of ACF/CCF jargon.
- [ACF vs CCF: what's the difference?](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/acf-vs-ccf.html): community-based vs school-based cadets.
- [How to join the army cadets](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/how-to-join-the-army-cadets.html): step by step — finding a detachment or school contingent, the first parade night, costs, what to bring.
- [What age can you join the cadets?](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/what-age-to-join-cadets.html): typical joining ages for ACF (around 12) and CCF (often around Year 9).
- [Cadet training subjects explained](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/cadet-training-subjects.html): what each of the 13 syllabus subjects covers.
- [Cadet star levels & ranks explained](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/cadet-star-levels-and-ranks.html): progression from Basic to 4-Star, and how cadet ranks work.
- [Cadet drill commands explained](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/cadet-drill-commands-explained.html): cautionary vs executive commands, the common static and marching orders.
- [Map reading: grid references](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/map-reading-grid-references.html): eastings and northings, four-figure and six-figure references, common mistakes.
- [How to revise for cadet assessments](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/how-to-revise-for-cadet-assessments.html): active recall and spaced practice applied to cadet training.
- [A parent's guide to Cadet AI](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/parents-guide-to-cadet-ai.html): safety, privacy and what the app does.
- [What do cadets actually do?](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/what-do-cadets-actually-do.html): a typical parade night, weekends and annual camp, the training subjects and qualifications on offer.
- [Army, air or sea cadets: which to join?](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/army-air-sea-cadets-compared.html): how the ACF, RAF Air Cadets, Sea Cadets and the school-based CCF differ. Note: Cadet AI covers the ACF/CCF syllabus, so it is much less useful to Air or Sea Cadets.
- [Cadet kit list: what to take](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/cadet-kit-list.html): what is issued vs bought, and what to pack for parade nights, weekends and camp.
- [The Duke of Edinburgh's Award and cadets](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/dofe-and-cadets.html): how DofE fits alongside cadet training and how cadet activities count towards the four sections.
- [Cadet uniform and inspection](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/cadet-uniform-and-inspection.html): what inspectors look for, boots, badges and turnout.
- [How to become a cadet force adult volunteer](https://cadetai.co.uk/guides/cadet-force-adult-volunteer.html): the CFAV role, vetting, training and time commitment. No military background needed.
